jobs.title: Contra Costa County Program Director
jobs.description:
Patients’ Right Program Director (Contra Costa County)

Department:
Directorate Team

Reports To:
Deputy Director

FLSA Status:
Full time, Exempt

Work Location:
In Office; 1350 Arnold Dr, Suite 200, Martinez, CA 94553; Contra Costa County Office.

Schedule:
Full-time, typically Monday- Friday; 37.5 hours per week. Additional hours as required to meet hearing coverage, reporting deadlines and contract requirements.

Position Summary

The Patients' Rights Program Director is accountable for protecting and advancing the statutory and constitutional rights of behavioral health clients served under the Contra Costa County Office of Patients' Rights contract. This role leads program strategy, staff performance, contract compliance, reporting, and stakeholder engagement. The Director ensures advocacy is timely, client-directed, and fully compliant with Welfare and Institutions Code, California Code of Regulations, and County policies.

Leadership Expectations

Set the standard for advocacy quality, responsiveness, and professionalism across the program.
Run a disciplined compliance calendar and hold staff accountable to deadlines.
Build strong county and facility relationships without compromising program independence.
Operate as a risk manager: identify issues early and drive corrective action fast.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Ensure program compliance with all applicable Welfare and Institutions Code requirements, California Code of Regulations, and County policies related to patients' rights advocacy.
Lead and supervise supervisors and advocates, including hiring, onboarding, training, scheduling, and performance management.
Ensure timely access standards are met for clients contacting the program directly and through facility referrals.
Oversee advocacy work including Certification Review hearings and other legal proceedings; ensure advocates represent clients' expressed interests.
Oversee investigation and resolution of patients' rights complaints at the lowest level possible and in a timely manner; ensure escalations follow policy.
Ensure completion of monthly and quarterly reports and submission of required attachments to the County, including staff rosters as required.
Ensure Adverse Incident Reports and other reportable event documentation are submitted within 24 hours when required and that corrective actions are tracked.
Lead required outreach activities, including providing patients' rights advocacy training at ED, acute, sub-acute, and residential settings at least twice annually, and annual board and care visits with maintained findings database.
Conduct quarterly input sessions with clients, families, direct care staff, and community partners; provide summary and follow-up plan to the County each quarter.
Represent SWS at County provider meetings and workgroups; ensure program remains current on updates issued through those forums.
Oversee data integrity and equity-focused quality improvement, including analysis to ensure outcomes are not driven by protected characteristics.
Ensure compliance with County requirements related to GenAI technology use and reporting, including notification and discontinuation if directed by the County.
Serve as program spokesperson as assigned; manage stakeholder relationships with hospitals, EDs, and community partners.
Coordinate with leadership on budget, staffing plans, and risk management.
Other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

Minimum 5 years experience in patients' rights advocacy, mental health law, healthcare compliance, or a closely related field, including at least 3 years in a leadership role.
Strong working knowledge of LPS processes, hearings, and patients' rights statutory framework.
Proven staff leadership skills, including coaching, corrective action, and building a high-performance culture.
Ability to produce clear written reports and maintain audit-ready documentation.
Strong judgment, discretion, and ability to manage confidential information.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and ability to learn required county systems and reporting tools.
Valid California driver license and proof of auto insurance; ability to travel to facilities across the county.
Successful completion of DOJ background check.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree in a relevant field (law, public health, healthcare administration) or equivalent experience.
Experience working with County behavioral health systems and contract monitoring.

Work Environment

This is primarily an in-person position.
Regular in-person attendance is required at assigned program locations, facilities, community meetings, trainings, and other work-related sites.
With supervisory approval, the employee may work from an approved home office for up to two days per week.
Home-office days are intended primarily for administrative duties, including:
Documentation
Reporting
Scheduling
Correspondence
Other related administrative tasks
The employee must remain available and responsive during all scheduled work hours.
On-site attendance may be required on a scheduled home-office day due to:
Meetings
Staffing needs
Training
Facility matters
Emergencies
Other operational priorities
The home-office arrangement is not guaranteed and may be modified or discontinued based on program or organizational needs.

Physical Requirements

Ability to sit for extended periods, travel, and perform facility walk-throughs; ability to lift up to 25 pounds.

Compliance and Performance Expectations

Protect the client’s voice and client choice, while remaining within legal and role boundaries.
Maintain strict confidentiality and comply with HIPAA and county privacy requirements.
Meet all reporting deadlines; late reporting is a compliance risk and will be addressed as performance.
Follow SWS Employee Handbook policies on conduct, attendance, technology use, and safety.
Use only approved technology to store, transmit, or process client information.

jobs.title: COO
jobs.description:
Chief Operating Officer — Urban Youth Collaborative (UYC)
Reports to: Chief Executive Officer
Location: Flexible within the U.S. (West Coast or Southeastern US preferred); candidates based in other regions with strong remote leadership skills will also be considered.

ABOUT URBAN YOUTH COLLABORATIVE

Urban Youth Collaborative exists to transform public school campuses into communities of faith, hope, and love by spreading the gospel of Jesus Christ through reproducing disciple-makers among the next generation. Through campus clubs, chaplaincy programs, community service projects, and sexual risk avoidance education, UYC empowers students to lead with purpose, build healthy relationships, and discover their God-given potential. With active ministry presence in San Diego (CA), Spokane (WA), Greater Sacramento (CA), Columbia (SC), Atlanta (GA), Tijuana (MX), and Addis Ababa (ET) — and emerging locations worldwide — UYC currently reaches approximately 8,000 students per week across these locations.

To see UYC's work firsthand, watch our ministry overview video (YouTube Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hHEz7lu6zu4) and explore our website: https://uyc.org/.

ROLE SUMMARY

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) serves as a key executive leader responsible for building and strengthening the operational infrastructure that fuels UYC's mission. The COO will oversee organization-wide systems, HR, program execution, media and outreach integration, and staff communication while ensuring operational excellence across multiple city expressions as the ministry grows. This leader brings strong strategic execution skills paired with a passion for youth ministry and collaborative leadership.

This role reports to and partners with the CEO, pursuing all initiatives under the CEO's direction, authority, and vision — this is a second-in-command position, not an independent executive seat.

This role also includes a personal fundraising requirement: the COO fundraises 10% of salary during year two of the position, 15% during year three, and 20% by year four (this requirement may be waived for a candidate who brings exceptional experience, fit, and value to the role).

This role requires agreement with UYC's Statement of Faith.

This role requires completion of UYC's full employment application, which includes questions on church commitment and spiritual history, and requires background check and credit report consent, and references including a church leader reference.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Organizational Leadership & Strategy
- Partner with the CEO in organizational planning, decision-making, and execution. Pursue all initiatives under direction, authority, and in alignment with the CEO's vision and in conversation with key ministry advisors.
- Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of scalable systems and structures as UYC expands nationally and internationally.
- Steward operational priorities to ensure alignment with mission and strategic growth.

Program Oversight
- Support and manage teams implementing Sexual Risk Avoidance Education (SRAE) programs in San Diego, CA and Columbia, SC, ensuring compliance, excellence, and goal achievement. UYC plans to pursue SRAE funding in Spokane, WA, when funds are released in 2027.
- Support program delivery, resource distribution, and reporting across City locations, working alongside the CEO, who is directly involved in City Director coaching during this season of growth.
- Assist the CEO in determining priorities for staffing and funding C-Suite and other organizational support roles as UYC grows gradually, including a future field staff oversight role.

Staff Management & HR Systems
- Oversee and expand HR operations, including hiring, onboarding, benefits administration, performance management, and staff culture/communication flow.
- Identify and implement a single staff health insurance plan that all employees can participate in and develop other employee benefits over time.
- Lead migration from 401K to 403B retirement plan.
- Assist CEO in determining priorities for HR staffing/firm partnership as UYC grows.
- Maintain organizational compliance with applicable local, state, and federal employment regulations.

Reporting & Accountability
- Work with teams to update UYC's Case for Support, Annual Report, and other high-level impact reports for the CEO and stakeholders as needed.
- Evaluate and approve city, employee, and event budgets to ensure positive cash flow.
- Establish KPI dashboards and evaluation systems that guide data-informed decisions.

UYC Media, Communications & Outreach
- Oversee brand consistency and integration of media and outreach initiatives throughout the organization, in conversation with the Development Director, as the organization grows.
- Ensure effective communication pathways across all departments and geographic locations.

National Expansion & LLC Management
- Inherit and gradually scale the operational frameworks for new UYC LLC locations.
- Work with the Executive Team, alongside the CEO's direct coaching relationship with City Directors, to support performance, growth, and sustainable ministry operations as UYC grows.

Advise on Grant & Funding Opportunities
- Share funding ideas with CEO, Grants Manager, and Development Director about capital and partnership opportunities worth pursuing for UYC.
- Provide introductions to potential funders when appropriate, as God leads.

Systematize Training, Certification, and Background Check Process
- Partner with the data team to roll out a nationwide and global system for church partners to become trained, certified, and complete background checks.

Envision Possibilities and Connect New National and Global Partners to UYC
- Build like-minded partnerships with US and international groups that align with UYC vision and mission as opportunities present themselves.
- Assist the CEO with expansion priorities and discernment based on the opportunities that God provides.
- All partnerships must be compatible with UYC's God-given mission and vision.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required
- Experience in nonprofit operations, administration, or executive leadership (5–10 years preferred)
- Proven ability to lead multi-site teams and manage organizational growth
- Strong HR, systems management, and compliance knowledge
- Demonstrated expertise with reporting, program oversight, and building operational infrastructure
- Excellent communication, decision-making, and relational leadership skills
- Passion for youth development, education, and faith-driven impact
- Agreement with UYC's Statement of Faith
- Fundraises 10% of salary during year two of position; 15% during year three; 20% by year four. This requirement may be waived for a person who brings exceptional experience, fit, and value to the role.

Preferred
- Experience overseeing federally or state-funded programs (e.g., SRAE)
- Multi-state nonprofit operations experience
- Background with ministry-based organizations or public school partnerships

Personal Characteristics
- Highly organized and detail-oriented
- Values-driven and mission-aligned
- A developer of people and systems
- Collaborative, humble, and courageous in leadership
- Deep Christian faith and passion for evangelism and disciple-making among youth
- Proven personal integrity, church commitment, and family-oriented life
- Track-record of stability in marriage/family, work relationships, finances, and personal health choices
- Able to thrive in a fast-growing, entrepreneurial ministry environment

WHAT UYC LOOKS FOR IN EVERY HIRE

UYC hires are expected to be humble in how they treat and interact with others, hungry in their willingness to take on significant needs with ambition, drive, and work ethic, and smart primarily in how they relate to and work with people rather than merely academically.

COMPENSATION

Salary range of $110,000–$125,000 based on experience, plus benefits including:
- Health insurance coverage
- Paid time off
- Professional development opportunities

Compensation for this role includes a personal fundraising component, consistent with UYC's staff support-raising model. UYC field staff carry significant fundraising responsibility as well; the COO's fundraising ramp (10%/15%/20% over years two through four) is lighter by comparison.

APPLICATION

Candidates should be prepared to complete UYC's full employment application, which includes questions on ministry and church background, spiritual history, management experience, fundraising experience and willingness, references (including a church leader reference), and background check and credit report consent, along with agreement to UYC's Statement of Faith.

Job Description

About The Fedcap Group

The Fedcap Group is a global nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing economic mobility, workforce development, education, and health through innovative, evidence-based solutions. Serving more than 332,000 people annually across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Australia, The Fedcap Group partners with government, employers, healthcare organizations, educational institutions, and community leaders to improve lives and strengthen communities.

Position Summary

The Chief Operating Officer, Fedcap Rehabilitation Services, is the senior executive responsible for leading the operational strategy, performance, and growth of Fedcap Rehabilitation Services, one of The Fedcap Group's largest organizations. Reporting to the President of Fedcap Rehabilitation Services. the COO provides executive leadership across a diverse portfolio of Total Facilities Management operations, revenue-generating and government-funded programs, workforce development initiatives, vocational rehabilitation services, and core operational functions that drive organizational performance while advancing the organization's mission and long-term sustainability.

The COO is responsible for translating strategic priorities into operational execution while driving growth, operational excellence, financial performance, exceptional service delivery, and customer satisfaction. This executive partners closely with the executive leadership team to strengthen organizational capabilities, expand strategic partnerships, foster innovation, and position the organization for sustainable growth and long-term impact.

The successful candidate is a seasoned operational leader with a proven track record of leading complex, multi-site organizations and large-scale Total Facilities Management operations. Experience should include facilities and engineering operations, building systems, janitorial services, property management, office services, print and mail operations, business solutions, or similar customer-focused service environments. The ideal candidate has successfully driven operational excellence, innovation, financial performance, and customer satisfaction across private, government, or other highly regulated sectors while advancing organizational mission and community impact.

Executive Responsibilities

Executive Leadership & Organizational Strategy

Partner with the President to establish and execute the organization's strategic vision, operational priorities, and long-term growth strategy.
Provide executive leadership across all operational functions to ensure organizational alignment, accountability, and execution.
Drive operational excellence through continuous improvement, innovation, and data-informed decision making.
Lead organizational transformation initiatives that improve efficiency, scalability, service quality, and business performance.
Establish performance expectations, monitor key metrics, and ensure achievement of operational and financial objectives.
Serve as a trusted advisor to the President, Board, and executive leadership team on operational strategy, business performance, and organizational opportunities.

Program Operations & Service Delivery

Oversee the performance, quality, and operational effectiveness of a diverse portfolio of Total Facilities Management operations, workforce development, vocational rehabilitation, and related service programs.
Ensure consistent execution of programs while improving customer experience, operational efficiency, and measurable outcomes.
Monitor operational performance through data, KPIs, and quality measures to drive continuous improvement.
Foster collaboration across operational teams to ensure consistent service delivery and organizational effectiveness.

Government Contracts, Compliance & Quality

Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, local, contractual, regulatory, and accreditation requirements.
Oversee quality assurance, risk management, contract performance, and operational compliance across the organization.
Promote a culture of accountability, ethical leadership, and continuous quality improvement.

Business Growth & Strategic Partnerships

Support organizational growth through operational expansion, innovation, and strategic initiatives.
Build and strengthen strategic partnerships that enhance organizational performance, business development, and community impact.
Collaborate with executive leadership to identify new opportunities that advance the organization's mission and long-term sustainability.
Represent the organization with key external stakeholders to strengthen partnerships, expand opportunities, and advance organizational objectives.

Financial & Operational Excellence

Partner with finance leadership to develop and manage operating budgets while ensuring strong financial stewardship.
Drive operational productivity, resource optimization, and financial performance across the organization.
Oversee monthly, quarterly, and annual budget reviews.
Monitor organizational performance using data and operational metrics to improve efficiency, effectiveness, and long-term sustainability.
Ensure operational resources, systems, and infrastructure support continued organizational growth.

People Leadership & Organizational Culture

Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing executive and operational leadership team.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
Build organizational capability through leadership development, succession planning, and talent optimization.
Champion employee engagement while reinforcing The Fedcap Group's mission, values, and culture.
Partner with the Board of Directors and executive leadership to advance the organization's strategic priorities and mission.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree preferred in Business or a related Human Services field.
Ten or more years of executive leadership experience leading and scaling complex organizations, preferably in both commercial and mission-driven environments.
Extensive executive leadership experience managing large-scale Total Facilities Management operations or similarly complex service organizations, including facilities management, engineering systems, building operations, janitorial services, property management, office services, print and mail operations, business solutions, or related operational functions.
Demonstrated success driving business growth, operational excellence, financial performance, customer experience, and organizational transformation.
Strong business and financial acumen with experience operating across diverse business and funding models.
Proven ability to develop high-performing leadership teams and lead organizations through growth, change, and continuous improvement.
Experience overseeing complex operations, regulatory compliance, quality, risk management, and operational performance.
Demonstrated success building strategic partnerships that advance organizational performance and growth.
Exceptional executive presence with outstanding communication, relationship-building, and influencing skills.

What Success Looks Like

High-performing Total Facilities Management, rehabilitation, and workforce development operations that consistently achieve operational, contractual, and financial goals.
Strong financial stewardship and effective management of organizational resources.
Exceptional program quality, regulatory compliance, and performance outcomes.
Trusted partnerships with government agencies, employers, educational institutions, customers, and community organizations.
Engaged, accountable, and high-performing operational leadership team.
Innovative, participant-centered programs and operational services that improve employment outcomes, customer satisfaction, and advance economic mobility.

Compensation & Benefits

Compensation: $200,000-$250,000 Annually

We are an EEO employer committed to diversity, M/F/D/V.

About Us

To create opportunities for people with barriers to economic well-being.

In 1935, Fedcap Rehabilitation Services was founded by three men in NYC who had sustained injuries in WWI and literally changed the world for people with physical disabilities. It now provides an array of services to youth and adults helping thousands each year graduate from high school, obtain vocational certification or a college degree, become work ready, obtain meaningful employment and achieve long term economic well-being.

jobs.description:
Job Description

POSITION OBJECTIVE
The Executive Director for Medical Development has primary responsibility to provide the strategic leadership of a comprehensive advancement program for the Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine's highest strategic priorities that impact the school's future and national reputation. The executive director is responsible for leading the national and international leadership gifts program, which includes major and principal gift strategies and opportunities. The executive director is responsible for the development of overall fundraising plans for the strategic priorities in alignment with the overarching strategies of the School of Medicine and the university's division of university relations and development. As an experienced development professional, the executive director is expected to engage in direct face-to-face cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of donors, and collaborate with university relations and development in developing strategies for the university's fundraising, alumni, annual fund and communications programs, and plan and implement initiatives for the medical school's highest priorities, national and international development, and major and principal gifts and the annual giving program.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS
Serve as a member of the executive management group of the School of Medicine's development and alumni relations office. Assist with the development and implementation of strategies and plans to fulfill the school's mission. (10%)
Work in partnership with the vice dean for development and alumni relations to develop and execute strategies targeted at the highest-level donors and prospects for the School of Medicine. (10%)
Provide leadership on fundraising plans and strategies for the School of Medicine's highest priorities including but not limited to scholarship, research funding, professorships, and specific inter-professional initiatives. (20%)
Develop and implement a strategic plan for the national and international development program that will encompass all areas of principal gifts, major gifts, annual giving, foundation relations corporate relations, alumni relations, special events and communications. (15%)
Manage a discreet portfolio of high-capacity prospective donors to maximize gifts from the School of Medicines¿ individual and foundation constituents. (10%)

NONESSENTIAL FUNCITONS
Lead and manage the medical school's Leadership Prospect Group meetings and develop/ execute high-level strategies to advance the school's major and principal gift pipeline, advising and coaching development staff. (5%)
Work in partnership with the university president, dean, vice president of health sciences, vice dean of development and alumni relations for the school of medicine and alumni relations and development colleagues and faculty of the school of medicine, and university relations and development to raise philanthropic support for priority programs, centers and departments. (5%)
Collaborate with the development and alumni relations staff to formulate an annual fundraising plan that articulates prospects to be seen, solicited and funds to be raised f for the dean, vice president and vice dean. (5%)
Collaborate with the development and alumni relations and central development staff in the implementation of the major components of a multimillion-dollar comprehensive campaign: including strategic planning, oversight, management, performance measurement and solicitation strategies. (5%)
Operate effectively, both as an individual and in a team environment, under the pressures of a major fundraising effort. (5%)
Establish and execute identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship activities for the school of medicine's strategic priorities to ensure lasting relationships with donors and potential donors. (5%)
Represent the school in its relationships with its development partners at the University Hospitals of Cleveland, Metro Hospital and the Cleveland Clinic. (2.5%)
Provide leadership to the development program and faculty of the School of Medicine to inform and educate multiple constituents about the accomplishments of the school of medicine. (2.5%)
Perform other duties as assigned. (<1%)

CONTACTS
Department: Frequent contact with dean and vice president of medical affairs, vice presidents, vice deans, associate deans, department chairs, and directors. Contact with faculty staff as required to perform essential functions.
University: Frequent collaboration with the senior vice president for university relations and development, including regular contact with the President's Office, vice presidents, deans, vice deans, trustees, and alumni. Contact with directors of administrative departments, faculty and staff as required to perform essential functions.
External: Daily contact with donors, alumni, foundation representatives, community organizers/advocates, corporate executives and federal, state and local government officials. Contact with foreign visitors, healthcare officials and academic boards and organizations as required to perform essential functions.
Students: Contact with undergraduate, graduate and professional students as required to perform essential functions.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES
Supervise a staff of seven development professionals and fundraisers and one administrative assistant.

QUALIFICAITONS
Experience: 10 or more years of progressive experience in development or related field with transferrable skills and a corresponding record of accomplishment in closing major gifts required.
Education: Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree preferred.

REQUIRED SKILLS
Demonstrated strategic management skills to successfully develop and implement a development plan. Significant demonstrated experience in leadership level individual giving to provide the leadership for the entire program.
Ability to meet consistent attendance.
Experience in medical affairs and biomedical research is desirable; experience in the grateful patient arena is highly desirable.
High degree of energy, creativity, flexibility, organization and interpersonal skills as well as excellent verbal and written communication skills required.
Must be able to work both independently and collaboratively with colleagues. Ability to interact with colleagues, supervisors, and customers face to face.
Computer proficiency (including Microsoft Office) and the ability to learn new programs.
Ability to demonstrate successful support, education, and advocacy for all students, aligned with the values, mission, and messaging of the university, while adhering to the staff policy on conflict of commitment and interest.
Willingness to learn and work with artificial intelligence (AI) tools and technologies.

WORKING CONDITIONS
General office environment, some evening and weekend work hours will be required. Frequent travel required.
Hybrid Eligibility

This position is eligible for hybrid work arrangement up to two remote days per week at the discretion of the department. New employees may begin a hybrid schedule upon approval from the supervisor, successful completion of an orientation period and signing the remote work checklist certification form.

jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Trust for Public Land (TPL) is the leader of a movement to connect everyone in America to the outdoors. A national nonprofit, TPL partners with communities to create high-quality parks and protect public lands—especially in communities that need them most—to improve public health, create social cohesion, strengthen historic and cultural connection to place, and increase climate resilience. Since 1972, TPL has protected more than 4 million acres of public land, created more than 5,500 parks, trails, schoolyards, and iconic outdoor places, generated over $112 billion in public funding for parks and public lands, and connected nearly 10 million people to the outdoors. To learn more, visit www.tpl.org.

“For over 50 years, Trust for Public Land has been working tirelessly towards our vision that every individual should have close-to-home access to the benefits of nature. In today’s world, our land-for-people solutions are even more relevant than ever. Quality parks and natural spaces are a fundamental requirement for sustaining healthy, equitable communities that are resilient and prepared for change. Parks and public lands connect us to each other and to the outdoors. As we enter our fifth decade, we have much to celebrate and even more promising work to pursue. We are a vibrant organization with a new strategic plan that builds on our success. Join us to become part of a growing and forward-thinking team focused on growing our philanthropic partnerships to ensure healthy, livable communities for generations to come.”

Patricia Watson, Chief Advancement Officer

Position Summary:

Reporting directly to the Pacific Region Director of Philanthropy, the Northwest Director of Philanthropy will be responsible for building relationships with and securing six- and seven-figure major gifts from high net-worth individuals located in across the two state region (Washington and Oregon) in support of the Northwest program, the Pacific Region, and the organization’s highest priorities and initiatives. The position is responsible for directly overseeing a portfolio of individuals, corporate, and foundations, with an emphasis on individual high-capacity major gift prospects and donors.

50% Relationship Manager: Manage a portfolio of approximately 100 donors and prospects with an emphasis on individual major gift ($100K+) donor prospects. Creates comprehensive engagement strategies, leads cultivation teams, and leads in the creation and delivery of final solicitation and stewardship materials. Promotes blended gifts, planned giving, and involves peer volunteers, executive leadership, senior management, and project staff in cultivation as needed.

30% Program Oversight: Oversee and accountable for all fundraising activities in the Northwest program. Ability to organize and motivate others, including peers and volunteers.

JOB DETAILS

Position Overview

The Executive Director is responsible for leading the entire community and supervising all community associates. This includes ensuring there is a positive and safe work environment in which residents are excited to live and team members are excited to work. This position reports to the Regional Vice President.

Key Business Areas

Morning Pointe has identified key business areas that will delineate the Executive Director areas of responsibility. Obviously, not all aspects of the position’s roles and responsibilities can be incorporated in this list.

Marketing And Community Relations

The ED is the sales leader for the community and will maintain target census level by creating a community sales culture and implementing external marketing plan.
Provide daily hands-on leadership in setting and executing sales goals and initiatives based on the company’s sales program; ensuring community meets sales Key Performance Indicators.
Participate in special events, marketing efforts and special programs, externally, as well as conducts tours to prospective families and residents.
Train all Directors and receptionists on conducting tours in the absence of the Executive Director or Community Relations Director.
Create, maintain, and ensure a positive environment throughout the community for residents, family, friends, and all team members, in alignment with the mission of Morning Pointe.
Promote positive image and build relationships to ensure favorable community relations.
Maintain current competitive analysis for utilization when developing budgets and to maintain competitive knowledge.
Participate in all new resident move-ins, including contract signing.

Financial Performance

Review at least monthly community revenue reporting, manage community budget and analyze financial statements, maintain budget accountability, anticipate and minimize negative budget variances and deficits; successfully manage operating expenses.
Accountable for meeting Net Operating Income (NOI) goals and budgeted revenue goals as defined by annual budget; review rent roll monthly at a minimum.
Implement monthly budgets for each department and ensure spend-downs are maintained.

General / Leadership

High moral and ethical values.
Responsibilities include supervision and quality control for all aspects of operations including marketing, staffing, resident care and services, budgeting, safety and building maintenance.
Ensure that the director team and associates maintain an environment which focuses on delivery of services by promoting individual resident capabilities through coordination of operations and programming functions for all departments.
Ensure that resident’s rights are well established and maintained at all times.
Ensure successful implementation of policies, procedures, and programs within the guidelines of state regulations and Morning Pointe policies.
Monitor resident, family, and associate satisfaction. Review complaints and grievances and makes written reports of action taken. Discuss such actions with appropriate parties.
Lead the community’s strategic planning initiative to establish goals and objectives in response to corporate goals.
Provide leadership, training and direction to the community leadership team and create annual development plans for each Director.
Inform supervisor and appropriate corporate office associates of any concerns related to the community, residents, or associates. Create reporting structure during absence of Executive Director.
Provide recognition and promote a positive and engaging culture for team members, residents, and families.
Strive to maintain a safe working environment through the prevention of accidents, the preservation of equipment, and the achievement of safe working practices.
Ensure that adequate supplies and equipment are on hand to meet the day-to-day operational needs of the community and residents.
With approval from management, responsible for securing annual Continuing Education Units required by the state to hold the appropriate administrator state license (if applicable) as a Morning Pointe Executive Director. Attend all required training, in-service, and staff meetings; participate in workshops, seminars, etc., to keep abreast of current data affecting senior living facilities, as well as to maintain a professional status.

Staff Management

Recruit, hire, retain, and coach high quality teams.
Ensure implementation of Morning Pointe staffing model and schedule labor hours consistent with staffing model (minimizing overtime) including proper level of staffing at all times.
Provide leadership and direction to all Directors and provide feedback concerning the operation of their departments to assist in eliminating/correcting problem areas, and/or improvement of services.
Lead staff meetings to ensure that appropriate information sharing is provided on a continuous basis.
Conduct operation meetings with Directors on a regular basis.
Maintain a cohesive team environment among departments.
Ensure appropriate new hire orientation and monthly in-service training for all associates is conducted while meeting state and corporate in-service training requirements.
Direct and evaluate management team during 90-day training period and annual review basis.
Approve and ensure that appropriate associate counseling and disciplinary actions occur.
Ensure that personnel files are created and maintained for all associates. Ensure record retention system meets state and corporate guidelines.
Review and approve bi-weekly payroll processing and ensure maintenance of appropriate documentation. Ensure record retention system meets state and corporate guidelines.
Ensure proper administration of Workers’ Compensation and Unemployment Compensation programs.
Participate and ensure required coverage for Manager on Duty program.
Establish proper reporting protocol is established in your absence.

Operations And Compliance

Assure compliance with local, state and federal regulations. Notify management of any visits by state officials. Give prompt attention to any cited deficiencies.
Support and successfully implement all Morning Pointe programs.
Approve all move-ins and move-outs.
Assist in preparing financial reports as requested.
Maintain records and investigate all incidents, accidents, or complaints.
Ensure maintenance of mandatory information, contracts, files, chemical specifications, and postings.
Review and approve all billing before forwarding to the Home Office.
Ensure maintenance of community Disaster Recovery Plan(s).
Ensure state regulations, company programs, policies and applicable guidelines are followed by associates, residents, visitors, and the general public.
Monitor resident care on a daily basis to ensure daily rounds and quality assurance programs are in place and enforced.
Establish and maintain a positive rapport with local and state agencies; ensure the community is survey ready at all times.

Resident Care

Responsible for ensuring specific programs, such as hydration, falls prevention, exercise and others as identified, are coordinated and implemented.
Ensure that Director of Nursing builds relationships and strong communication with residents and families to aid in the adjustment to Morning Pointe, identification of needs, concerns and appropriate service plan development for each resident.
Participate in care plan conferences as needed in coordination with Director of Nursing to review service plans with residents or families.
Ensure necessary ancillary services such as podiatry, dentistry, therapies, pharmacy consultation and similar services.

Resident Engagement

Ensure development of creative and exciting activity programming meeting Morning Pointe requirements with focuses on key aspects of healthy aging and individual preferences.
Conduct and/or arrange training to ensure all associates have an understanding of the purpose behind activity programming and special programs such as Morning Pointe in Motion, Meaningful Day, and Best Friends Approach.
Participate in activities calendar creation and ensure newsletters are distributed timely to newsletter database.

Dietary Services

Work collaboratively with Food Service Director to ensure dining services meets and/or improves targeted goals for food cost, food quality, and resident satisfaction.
Communicate resident dietary feedback to appropriate regional or corporate team members.

Asset Management

Ensure that the community, grounds, and property are maintained at the highest standard of excellence through preventative maintenance systems and programs. View the grounds and community through the eyes of a new visitor.
Routinely conduct community rounds with Maintenance Director.
Ensure work orders are completed timely to ensure a safe environment and satisfied customers.
Participate in interactive emergency drills. Ensure associates have a solid understanding of actions to be taken in emergency situation.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Demonstrated record of success in a leadership capacity.
Able to communicate effectively with all levels of associates, residents, family members, guests, vendors, referral sources, and the community at large.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; organizational and time management skills.
Intermediate level of computer and technology competency, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and other Microsoft Windows applications.
Passion for working with seniors.
Knowledge of customer service principles and practices.
Knowledge and understanding of the mission of Morning Pointe Senior Living.

Other Expectations

Perform other related essential duties as assigned.
Occasional travel is required and a valid driver’s license and proof of insurability is required.

Education And Experience Requirements

Bachelor's Degree in business administration, health care administration or other relevant course of study. Licensure required by state (if applicable).
Strong leadership skills with a minimum of two (2) years' experience in supervising and management.
A minimum of two (2) years' experience within a senior living environment or equivalent professional experience.
Required experience as an Executive Director in a healthcare setting

Physical Demands

Frequent lifting, carrying, pushing, pulling, stooping, bending, turning, and stretching. Finger and hand dexterity required. Visual and hearing acuity essential. Ability to understand and carry out written and oral instructions necessary. Ability to perform basic mathematical computations required

Brief Description

LaunchCode is looking for a Chief Development Officer to lead fundraising for Hire Human, our new national AI upskilling and job placement initiative. You will own fundraising strategy, major giving, and grant relationships end to end — helping us scale from serving thousands each year to tens of thousands. Strategic fundraising and earned revenue make our free, open-to-all programs possible. The momentum is already building. This year, we launched three in-house AI courses designed around employer demand. Nearly 5,000 people have engaged with our curriculum, and employers in our hiring network have already committed to hiring graduates. Now it’s time to scale.
You will lead a small team and have significant ownership over the future of development at LaunchCode. We’re a lean, remote nonprofit where everyone — including senior leaders — stays close to the work. We’re looking for a hands-on fundraiser who moves fast, builds relationships proactively, and thrives in the early stages of building something ambitious. Ideally, you’ll bring an established network of donors, foundations, and funders you can activate from day one. If you’re a builder who wants to create a national fundraising function — not inherit one — we want to hear from you.
Essential Duties/Responsibilities

Design and execute a multi-year national fundraising strategy for the Hire Human initiative, aligned to LaunchCode's national growth goals.
Lead major giving — build, manage, and close a personal portfolio of major donor and institutional relationships.
Own grant strategy and execution end to end: prospecting, proposal development, submission, award management, and reporting.
Manage and develop a small team for donor relations and grant support.
Build the relationships and pipeline needed to scale Hire Human from a regional to a national program.
Serve as the primary external face of LaunchCode for institutional funders and strategic partners, including travel as needed.
Collaborate with the executive and finance teams to integrate fundraising into overall organizational growth, revenue goals, and forecasting.

Demonstrated track record of personally closing six- and seven-figure gifts or grants
Experience building or scaling a development function, ideally in a lean or startup-like environment
Deep network of existing funder, foundation, and major donor relationships
Comfort operating with significant autonomy and limited layers of support
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including grant writing and donor-facing presentation
Passion for AI, continued learning and workforce development

9+ years of nonprofit development experience in progressively responsible leadership positions with at least 5 years in a senior leadership role, including direct responsibility for major gifts and grants

Experience fundraising for workforce development, education, or tech-sector nonprofits
Familiarity with national foundation and federal/state workforce funding landscapes (e.g., DOL/ETA)
Experience managing a small team through a period of rapid growth
Experience with Asana, AI tooling and HubSpot or similar CRM/fundraising tools

We value passion, drive, and aptitude over credentials and believe it is imperative that companies should, too. Want to learn more? 12 paid holidays and accrue 25 days of Paid Time Off per year
100% employer-funded medical, dental, and vision insurance premiums for employees and 75% employer-funded premiums for dependents
401k contribution match up to 6% after 6 months, immediate vesting
12 weeks of fully paid parental leave after 1 year

jobs.description:
Program Director, State-Sponsored Threats

At C4ADS, we are proving what is possible when open data, technology, and rigorous analysis are brought together to illuminate the illicit networks that threaten global peace and security. Our teams investigate complex transnational challenges, uncover connections that are often difficult to see, and translate evidence into actionable insights for partners across the public, private, and civil society sectors.

As the Program Director, State-Sponsored Threats, you will lead one of C4ADS’ core analytical programs focused on understanding and exposing the networks, actors, and systems that enable state-sponsored threats and related illicit activity.

You will report to the Senior Director for Analysis and be responsible for the strategic direction, analytical quality, people leadership, and overall performance of the program. You will lead and mentor a team of analysts, oversee a diverse portfolio of research and partner driven projects, manage donor relations and drive program funding, and help ensure that the program continues to produce rigorous, innovative, and impactful analysis.

This role is well suited for an experienced analytical leader who can move comfortably between strategy and execution. You will set priorities, develop people, manage complex portfolios, strengthen analytical approaches, and work across C4ADS to ensure the program’s research contributes meaningfully to our mission and the needs of our partners.

What You’ll Do

Lead the strategic direction and day to day management of the State-Sponsored Threats program
Manage, develop, and support a team of analysts working across multiple research portfolios and analytical projects
Establish program priorities and translate organizational strategy into clear research objectives, workplans, and deliverables
Oversee analytical production across the program, ensuring that research is rigorous, well sourced, timely, and consistent with C4ADS’ analytical standards
Provide substantive guidance and quality assurance on research products, publications, briefings, and partner deliverables
Coach and develop team members through clear expectations, ongoing feedback, mentorship, and professional development
Manage resources, timelines, competing priorities, and dependencies across a complex portfolio of projects
Identify opportunities to strengthen program operations, including project management, reporting, workflow design, knowledge management, and performance measurement
Manage and strengthen relationships with program donors

Translate complex research into clear, compelling findings for technical and nontechnical audiences
Represent the program through senior level briefings, partner engagements, and other external forums
Build and maintain trusted relationships with funders, research partners, subject matter experts, and other stakeholders
Ensure ongoing funding for the program and its priorities through identifying funding opportunities and drafting funding proposals in coordination with the Business Development team
Identify opportunities for collaboration across C4ADS programs and capabilities, recognizing where shared data, expertise, or methodologies can strengthen our collective impact
Work closely with the Senior Director for Analysis, analytical leadership, Business Development, Operations, and other teams to align program priorities, resources, partnerships, and organizational needs
Contribute to the broader strategic direction of C4ADS by identifying emerging threats, analytical opportunities, and areas where the organization can have meaningful impact

What We’re Looking For

We are looking for an experienced and thoughtful leader who is equally comfortable managing projects, donors and staff, shaping analytical strategy, and navigating complex research environments. You should bring strong judgment, intellectual curiosity, and a commitment to producing work that is analytically rigorous and useful to the audiences we serve.

Successful candidates will bring:

Demonstrated experience leading and developing high performing teams
Strong people management, project management, budget management, and organizational skills
Experience overseeing complex research portfolios with multiple stakeholders, priorities, and deadlines
Strong judgment and the ability to make thoughtful decisions in ambiguous or rapidly evolving environments
Experience conducting or overseeing open source or publicly available information research and analysis
A robust background investigating and addressing state sponsored threats from countries that may include Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea
A strong understanding of analytical methodologies, source evaluation, research design, and evidentiary standards
Experience working with data platforms, including Palantir Foundry 
Experience reviewing, editing, and strengthening complex analytical products
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to make complex findings accessible and relevant to different audiences
Experience developing and delivering senior level briefings
Experience working with a range of data sources, research methodologies, or analytical tools
A demonstrated ability to establish and maintain high standards for analytical rigor, sourcing, and quality
Strong relationship management skills and the ability to work effectively with internal and external partners, as well as donors
Experience fundraising, particularly in designing and drafting funding proposals 
Experience managing hiring processes
A collaborative mindset and an interest in working across disciplines, programs, and functional teams
Curiosity, creativity, initiative, and a willingness to challenge existing approaches in pursuit of better analysis
A commitment to C4ADS’ mission and an interest in using evidence driven analysis to address complex global security challenges
Legal and logistical ability to work onsite in C4ADS’ Washington, DC office a minimum of 2 days a week
Relevant language capabilities a plus but not a requirement

ABOUT URBAN YOUTH COLLABORATIVE

Urban Youth Collaborative exists to transform public school campuses into communities of faith, hope, and love by spreading the gospel of Jesus Christ through reproducing disciple-makers among the next generation. Through campus clubs, chaplaincy programs, community service projects, and sexual risk avoidance education, UYC empowers students to lead with purpose, build healthy relationships, and discover their God-given potential. Systematize Training, Certification, and Background Check Process
- Partner with the data team to roll out a nationwide and global system for church partners to become trained, certified, and complete background checks.

- Build like-minded partnerships with US and international groups that align with UYC vision and mission as opportunities present themselves.

Trust for Public Land (TPL) is the leader of a movement to connect everyone in America to the outdoors. High moral and ethical values.

At C4ADS, we are proving what is possible when open data, technology, and rigorous analysis are brought together to illuminate the illicit networks that threaten global peace and security. You will lead and mentor a team of analysts, oversee a diverse portfolio of research and partner driven projects, manage donor relations and drive program funding, and help ensure that the program continues to produce rigorous, innovative, and impactful analysis.

This role is well suited for an experienced analytical leader who can move comfortably between strategy and execution. Lead the strategic direction and day to day management of the State-Sponsored Threats program
Manage, develop, and support a team of analysts working across multiple research portfolios and analytical projects
Establish program priorities and translate organizational strategy into clear research objectives, workplans, and deliverables

Manage resources, timelines, competing priorities, and dependencies across a complex portfolio of projects
Identify opportunities to strengthen program operations, including project management, reporting, workflow design, knowledge management, and performance measurement
Manage and strengthen relationships with program donors

Translate complex research into clear, compelling findings for technical and nontechnical audiences
Represent the program through senior level briefings, partner engagements, and other external forums
Build and maintain trusted relationships with funders, research partners, subject matter experts, and other stakeholders

Identify opportunities for collaboration across C4ADS programs and capabilities, recognizing where shared data, expertise, or methodologies can strengthen our collective impact
